title: Programming Fundamentals
text: CS101 Programming Fundamentals. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: none. Introduces variables, control flow, functions, and testing.

title: Object-Oriented Programming
text: CS102 Object-Oriented Programming. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS101. Covers classes, inheritance, interfaces, and unit testing.

title: Data Structures
text: CS201 Data Structures. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS102 or instructor consent. Students implement lists, trees, graphs, and hash tables.

title: Algorithms
text: CS202 Algorithms. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS201 and MATH120. Analyzes algorithm design and complexity.

title: Database Systems
text: CS301 Database Systems. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS201 and MATH120. Covers relational modeling, SQL, transactions, and indexing.

title: Operating Systems
text: CS302 Operating Systems. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS201 or CS202. Covers processes, memory, file systems, and concurrency.

title: Computer Networks
text: CS303 Computer Networks. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS202 and either STAT201 or MATH220.

title: Software Engineering
text: CS304 Software Engineering. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS201 and CS202. Requires team project work.

title: Human Computer Interaction
text: CS305 Human Computer Interaction. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS201. Covers user research, prototyping, and usability evaluation.

title: Cloud Computing
text: CS306 Cloud Computing. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS201 or CS202. Introduces distributed services and deployment.

title: Security Fundamentals
text: CS307 Security Fundamentals. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS201. Covers authentication, authorization, and threat modeling.

title: Compiler Design
text: CS308 Compiler Design. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS202. Covers parsing, type checking, and code generation.

title: Advanced Systems
text: CS401 Advanced Systems. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS301 and CS302. Examines scalable storage and distributed systems.

title: Applied Software Project
text: CS402 Applied Software Project. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS304 and instructor consent.

title: Artificial Intelligence
text: AI410 Artificial Intelligence. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS401 and MATH220. Covers search, planning, and machine learning foundations.

title: Machine Learning
text: ML420 Machine Learning. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS202 and STAT201. Covers supervised learning, validation, and model evaluation.

title: Discrete Mathematics
text: MATH120 Discrete Mathematics. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: none. Covers logic, proof, sets, combinatorics, and graphs.

title: Linear Algebra
text: MATH220 Linear Algebra. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: MATH120. Covers vectors, matrices, eigenvalues, and applications.

title: Statistics for Computing
text: STAT201 Statistics for Computing. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: MATH120. Covers probability, estimation, inference, and regression.

title: Data Management
text: DS301 Data Management. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: CS201 and STAT201. Covers data cleaning, SQL pipelines, and governance.

title: Data Visualization
text: DS302 Data Visualization. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: STAT201 or CS201. Covers visual encodings, dashboards, and communication.

title: Applied Data Science
text: DS401 Applied Data Science. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: DS301 and DS302. Requires a documented analysis project.

title: Data Ethics
text: DS402 Data Ethics. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: none. Covers privacy, fairness, accountability, and responsible deployment.

title: Big Data Systems
text: DS403 Big Data Systems. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: DS301 or CS306. Covers distributed data processing and reliability.

title: Experiment Design
text: DS404 Experiment Design. Credits: 3. Prerequisites: STAT201. Covers causal questions, experiments, and interpretation.

title: Computer Science BSc Requirements
text: Computer Science BSc requires core programming, algorithms, systems, and a capstone. At least 30 credits must be completed in residence. Students should verify current elective offerings with the department.

title: Data Science BSc Requirements
text: Data Science BSc requires data management, statistics, visualization, and an applied project. The program includes 12 credits of approved electives. Students should verify current elective offerings with the department.

title: Academic Policies
text: Academic policy: a prerequisite may be satisfied by an approved equivalent or instructor consent when the department records that approval. The catalog does not state course availability by semester, instructor assignment, classroom, textbook, or delivery mode.
